column3: Whether the team learns from each sprint and shows it.
column6: Every sprint the team names one thing it learned and one process change it made because of it; the partner's feedback shows up in the next sprint's work, or the partner is told why not.
column9: The team reflects when asked and has acted on some of the partner's feedback; some sprints show a change, most do not.
column12: No reflection the partner can point to; the same feedback is given twice with no visible effect.

column3: Whether the team has written down what it is building, in terms the partner agreed to.
column6: The team has written, measurable goals the partner agreed to and a prioritized list the partner has seen; questions arrive before the work starts.
column9: Goals are written but some cannot be measured as written or carry no priority; the partner sometimes learns of an assumption after the fact.
column12: No written goals the partner has seen; the team builds on assumptions the partner never confirmed.

column3: Whether working software exists, advances, and can be run by someone other than the team.
column6: The partner can access working software every sprint; milestones are met or renegotiated ahead of time; decisions that affect the partner are explained before they are made.
column9: Progress is visible most sprints; some milestones slip without warning.
column12: Nothing runnable to show; progress is described, not demonstrated.

column3: Whether the team tests against a written approach the partner has seen, and collects and acts on feedback from the partner or users.
column6: The partner has seen a written test and validation approach; tests run on every change; feedback from the partner or from users is collected every sprint and visibly acted on.
column9: Tests cover some parts and run when someone remembers; feedback is collected some sprints.
column12: No tests the partner knows of; no feedback collected.

column3: Whether the whole team shows up, any member can answer for the project, and the work is visibly shared.
column6: The whole team attends, prepared; anyone can speak to the project; disagreements are resolved and reported to the partner; work is visibly spread across members.
column9: Most members attend most meetings; one or two members carry the meetings; disagreements show in a meeting and are settled by the next one.
column12: Members miss meetings without notice; one person does the talking and the work; conflict shows and nobody manages it.

column3: Whether the partner always knows where the project stands without asking.
column6: Every meeting has an agenda beforehand, hears from every student, and ends with notes afterward; demos show working software, and updates arrive on the agreed schedule.
column9: Most meetings have an agenda before and notes after; one or two students rarely speak; the partner occasionally has to chase an update.
column12: Meetings have no agenda or notes; the same one or two people speak; the partner chases for updates; demos are slides instead of running software.
